Lessons.Title: Ways to Find Unknown Length (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use the known attributes of two-dimensional figures (such as side lengths and symmetry) to reason about the perimeter of shapes.
In previous lessons, you examined the attributes of two-dimensional figures. You identified, sorted, and drew figures based on side length, angle size, presence of parallel or perpendicular sides, and symmetry. In this lesson, you use your understanding of these attributes to find the perimeter of different shapes.

2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Multiple Thirds (10 minutes); Activity 1: All the Way Around (20 minutes); Activity 2: Ponder Perimeter (15 minutes); Activity 3: Perimeter Expressions [OPTIONAL] (10 minutes); Cool-down: What's the Perimeter? (5 minutes)
Source-goal geometric reasoning: Perimeter is the sum of the actual outside side lengths; symmetry and equal lengths can supply otherwise unmarked sides.

Edulytics worked explanation: Read each original perimeter diagram and its units. Add only its exterior sides, using equal-side marks or symmetry where supported. For four outside lengths of 18, 26, 13 and 37 feet, the perimeter is 94 feet.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (not gated original): What is the perimeter of a triangle whose three sides are each 7 cm?
Original student diagrams, teacher card sorting, paper folding, and physical drawings require figure-by-figure / teacher validation.
